propositions: The 'undecomposed' hard-override axis fires on only 0.1% of verified findings (11/10250 plan-v3, 18/11773 plan-v4), two orders below other axes, despite flooring all non-none grades to impact 0.85.

The cited G5 deterministic suppressor (veto_undecomposed_g5) that justifies the low rate has never fired (0 instances across 2000 reviews) and cannot apply to 91% of reviewed tickets which have no children.

The grade-to-floor mapping is miscalibrated: 16 of 29 fires were 'low' grade, yet 25 of 29 were blocked only by the 0.85 floor with no other hard-override criterion present, meaning low grades produce hard blocks.

The inverse population (findings whose text matches flat-plan regex but scored undecomposed=none) contains 33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 entries, but sampling shows these are false positives matching code-decomposition prose rather than undecomposed plans.

The axis is neither working-as-intended nor unreachable, but exhibits the same miscalibration pattern previously fixed for ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation: ordinal-ladder grades flooring on their weakest value.
Follow-up story d4c2-b67e-ab99-4410 scoped to retune the floor to gate on medium+high grades, drop the inert G5 hedge from prompt text, and decide whether veto_undecomposed_g5 earns its keep.
